context_correction: The three oversized v1 recall cases are invalid and excluded. Their results were replaced with the corrected exact-length cases; all other vLLM payloads match the final frozen corpus.
limitations: Single-client latency benchmark; native requests queue behind one active generation. No new batched-throughput or endurance qualification.
RadixArk and Inferact are different quantizations. Dynamic FP4 activation prefill changes numerics; the sampled quality screen does not establish general quality equivalence.

Both engines use BF16 KV here; activation kernels, recurrent-state implementations, software versions, and memory pool sizes differ. vLLM allocates capacity for 538851 KV tokens; native allocates 65536.
Native DFlash2 only accelerates greedy requests. Model-default temperature remains 1.0; sampled requests fall back to target-only generation.
The fast native DFlash profile is compared with vLLM target-only; no vLLM DFlash result is claimed.
The host had pre-existing swap and some swap-in activity, with zero measured swap-out. CPU activity was not isolated; GPU jobs ran sequentially.
The current recipe CLI rejects existing host swap. Hardware verification used the advanced server command; admission behavior is tested separately.
Full Fast certification and a 60-minute endurance run remain outstanding.
